s1.syndrome_frame: Acute severe abdominal pain with nausea, transient loss of consciousness, and lethargy in a patient with a history of polycythemia vera and hypertension
key_facts: 14-year history of polycythemia vera
History of hypertension
Medications included aspirin, hydroxyurea, and intermittent losartan
Poor adherence to phlebotomies and other therapy
Blood pressure was 110/75 mmHg on arrival
Lethargic and confused on arrival
Chronic leukocytosis consistent with underlying disease
Abdominopelvic CT scan showed splenomegaly and bilateral adrenal masses
Adrenal masses were nonenhancing with an attenuation of 50 HU
No evidence of vascular thrombosis

shortlist.label: Adrenal Hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral adrenal masses with nonenhancing attenuation of 50 HU on CT scan

shortlist.label: Splenomegaly due to Polycythemia Vera
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a 14-year history of polycythemia vera and massive splenomegaly on CT scan

shortlist.label: Adrenal Cortical Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral adrenal masses with significant size increase on follow-up CT scan

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral adrenal masses in a patient with history of hypertension

shortlist.label: Splanchnic Vein Thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of polycythemia vera, which increases the risk of thrombosis, and presented with abdominal pain and splenomegaly

raw.rationale: The patient's acute severe abdominal pain, nausea, and transient loss of consciousness, combined with the presence of nonenhancing bilateral adrenal masses on CT scan, are consistent with adrenal hemorrhage, particularly in the context of a patient with a history of polycythemia vera and potential for bleeding complications due to aspirin use and poor adherence to phlebotomies.

rejected.label: Splenomegaly due to Polycythemia Vera
rejected.why: While splenomegaly is present and consistent with polycythemia vera, it does not directly explain the acute abdominal pain or the adrenal masses.

rejected.label: Adrenal Cortical Carcinoma
rejected.why: The nonenhancing nature of the adrenal masses and the acute presentation are not typical for adrenal cortical carcinoma, which usually presents with more chronic symptoms and has different imaging characteristics.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: The absence of hypertension crisis and the nonenhancing nature of the adrenal masses make pheochromocytoma less likely, as these tumors are typically hyperdense and associated with episodes of hypertension.

rejected.label: Splanchnic Vein Thrombosis
rejected.why: The absence of evidence of vascular thrombosis on the CT scan and the specific location of the masses in the adrenal glands rather than the splanchnic veins make this diagnosis less likely.
